headline: High: Gemini CLI can write/egress from shared files and MCP, creating dangerous default interaction risks with Airbyte’s broad networked data workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-driven data workflows and broad network egress, while Gemini CLI reads files/stdin and can use user-configured MCP tools. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct default channel is documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP server
IF Gemini CLI is prompted to treat Airbyte-produced text as instructions
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers for the pair
Keep Airbyte outputs in read-only export folders
Use a strict prompt wrapper that strips instructions from file content
Require manual review before Gemini CLI consumes Airbyte-generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Gemini CLI reads local files and sends requests to Google APIs or user MCP servers. If they share a workspace, sensitive business data can flow from Airbyte into Gemini CLI’s context and then out over network egress. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a directory Gemini CLI can read
IF Gemini CLI forwards that content to its backend or an MCP server
mitigations: Separate workspaces for Airbyte and Gemini CLI
Restrict Gemini CLI to non-sensitive directories
Turn off or review MCP servers before use
Redact business data before passing files between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; Airbyte also has broad network egress and API-driven workflows. The pair can concurrently mutate shared files or repo state, and Gemini CLI explicitly shares state via filesystem and git. That makes write conflicts dangerous by default when both operate on the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are edited while Gemini CLI is running
mitigations: Use separate repos or output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Enable git locks or branch-per-agent workflows
Run Gemini CLI in a sandboxed clone

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data artifacts that Gemini CLI may read from files and then act on through shell, git, or MCP tools. Because Gemini CLI has action-taking authority, unverified Airbyte outputs can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Airbyte-generated files as authoritative inputs
IF Gemini CLI executes shell or git actions based on those files without verification
mitigations: Add a verification step before Gemini CLI acts
Require human approval for shell and git actions
Mark Airbyte outputs as untrusted in the workflow
Use checksum or schema validation on exchanged files

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Gemini CLI handles local files and can send content to Google APIs or user MCP servers. If regulated business data is routed through Gemini CLI, retention or residency obligations may differ from Airbyte’s pipeline handling. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated business data is processed by both agents
IF Gemini CLI’s backend retention or residency differs from Airbyte’s data handling policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to Gemini CLI
Keep regulated datasets out of Gemini CLI workflows
Review retention settings for Gemini CLI accounts
Document a data-processing agreement for shared workflows
